title: Gregory of Nyssa, Against Eunomius (1)
english: The work of Gregory of Nyssa likewise, on behalf of Basil against Eunomius, has been read by me. In expression — an orator if ever there was one — he is brilliant, preserving ever what gives delight, yet even he does not refute Eunomius's writing point by point in order. Hence he is more concise than Theodore, but fuller than Sophronius; he abounds in reflections and examples. One may say without fear that as far as he outstrips Theodore in beauty, brilliance, and utmost sweetness, so far does Theodore outstrip him in the number of his arguments, straining whatever is fruitful into service of the point at hand.
translator_notes: Greek locked from Bekker 1824; Freese 1920 used as PD English reference only.
Codex 6 of 279; Gregory of Nyssa (c. 335–395), bishop of Nyssa, younger brother of Basil the Great. 'Enthymeme' = rhetorical syllogism from probable premises.
